question.knowledge_point: Finding the Points of Intersection of a Horizontal Line and a Tangent Curve
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14040762/assets/f00d8bd6cbd1f113df7f023e161e4d79e2f4a81157d1ac9a8ab65e70b4959221.png)

The graph above shows the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.$  Find the $x$-coordinate of the point $B.$
question.worked_solution:
The $y$-values of both functions are the same at the intersection point. Equating the two equations gives: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}
$$

 Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})=-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

This value lies inside $-\pi \le x<\pi $ hence, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{6}.$ This is the $x$ coordinate of $A.$

To get another solution, we add $\pi $ to the principal value. Thus,

$$
{x}_{2}=\pi +x=\pi -\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{5\pi }{6}.
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of $B$ is $\frac{5\pi }{6}.$
